benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Fell for a third straight session to $97.95 on 6 Oct (Trading Economics), as markets weighed a reported Saudi-backed advance toward Bab el-Mandeb/Mocha and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline ramping above 80% of capacity against a still-closed Hormuz. Week-ago uses 1 Oct (5 days prior) — the closest dated figure found this run, not a full week.

benchmarks.label: WTI

peak.note: EIA Cushing spot high via FRED.

benchmarks.note: Fell for a third straight session to $87.32 on 6 Oct, the lowest since early September (Trading Economics), as recovering Saudi Red Sea exports and G7 reserve releases outweighed renewed Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb risk. Week-ago uses 1 Oct (5 days prior) — the closest dated figure found this run, not a full week.

benchmarks.label: TTF gas
benchmarks.note: Rose 3.9% to €76.38 on 6 Oct, a two-week high, on continued risk to Hormuz LNG flows (Trading Economics). Week-ago uses 5 Oct (1 day prior) — the closest dated figure found this run, not a full week. Pre-crisis €32.00 is derived from RTÉ's figure of +€14.52 to €46.52 on 2 March.

benchmarks.label: Henry Hub
benchmarks.note: NYMEX front-month was $3.08 on 6 Oct (Trading Economics), up on expectations of cooler weather lifting heating demand. Week-ago uses 5 Oct (1 day prior) — the closest dated figure found this run, not a full week; pre-crisis is the EIA spot price on 27 Feb (FRED). US LNG feedgas and exports are near records, but the US price is largely insulated.
